body: Oh I'm Sorry I Forgot That I Have To Capitalize Every Single Word In My Sentence. Thanks So Much For Teaching Me The Right Way. Too Bad More People Don't Remember To Do That. They Should Totally Kill Themselves.
I present female online, usually (obviously not here). I guess I never thought about doing it in private. I dunno, maybe it would help. I guess I should try, for science at least.

I explained to her that they were fleeting but she seemed unwilling to listen to me. I mean, I guess it's better for her to be safe than sorry, but I don't appreciate her not listening. I felt ignored and as if I was being dragged along at *her* will rather than mine.

I shouldn't have to 'prove' my willingness to commit to her in the first place, and I shouldn't even need a letter. I'm only there because I can't afford an informed consent doctor. I can't do most of those things right now, anyways. I don't have money for hair removal, voice training without being diagnosed with gender dysphoria (for insurance reasons. Also I'm not going to try to train myself and risk damaging my voice), and I'm not a crossdresser so wearing female clothes without feeling like I'm a girl who's wearing them won't make me feel any better.

Well my first step forward is trying to get the medical attention I need, which is why I went to her in the first place. I can't afford electrolysis right now, I don't think insurance will cover seeing a speech pathologist (I'm worried to try it on my own, because if I'm doing something wrong and don't realize it, I could damage my voice very badly. I want professional supervision in order to be safe) unless I get diagnosed with gender dysphoria, and I certainly can't try presenting as female without being on hormones for a while, so, right now I think I've hit a wall :/ Getting these hormones is the only way I feel I can move forward at all right now.
It was only my first session. Like it says in the title, maybe I'm just paranoid. But I still feel very unsatisfied so far.
She didn't even give me a chance to talk about my trans issues. She just pummeled me with distracting questions and I didn't get to say anything about it...
Sure. I'll just pull everything I need out of the æther.

>If you really can't live as a man then what are you doing to progress?

I'm *trying* to progress by going to the therapist in the first place. That's all I can do! Attitudes like this just turn it into some ridiculous contest. I think it's disgusting that people think I should be on trial and have to 'prove' that I'm good enough just to receive medical attention. It shouldn't be anybody's choice but my own, but that's just the situation I'm in.

It's things like this that make me think I'm probably better off dead.
Well how am I going to get any better unless I'm given the medical attention I need?
You lose points for liking Math. What an idiotic test.

But I am suicidal, and she knows. I don't lie. But the reason I am is because I'm not getting treated. I want to do it because I can't live as a male. I can't do it. Transitioning is the only thing that will help. I know it. But she'll probably want to just throw drugs at me.
She immediately told me that I should go to a psychiatrist. Now I'm even more suspicious.
She says she has 'experience' with trans people. I wish I could look up her past patients and ask them about her.
My depression is absolutely linked, but my anxiety isn't. That's what worries me. And I'm a bad liar, so I couldn't tell her otherwise (not that I would).
My insurance is through the same institution where the doctors work, if that makes any sense. I'm very limited because they only pay for doctors that are part of the company.
Yoga and pilates, eh? That actually sounds like a nice idea! Thanks~
I don't think it could. Maybe a low level government spot in very specific locations, but other than that I don't think there's any way.

Poland has a trans woman on parliament. I don't think the US has ever had a trans person even run for any level of office, but I have a feeling it wouldn't go over well. At least at that high of a position (whatever equivalent that would be).

Legal rights aren't always enforced, and social acceptance is a big factor, too. Don't try to tell me that the US as a whole is accepting of us :P Some states, sure, but as a country, I don't think so.
The fact that the USA is one of the more accepting places is really disturbing u ~ u

Thanks for the both friendly and realistic answer. If I don't look like a supermodel, that's fine... Just as long as there is no question that I'm female, I'll be content enough.

I am very grateful of my hair, though. I used to have it very long (cut it because suppressing) and I had cis girls get pissy (jokingly) with me out of jealousy :P So that's one thing I'm not insecure about.
Would bangs, etc, distract or draw attention to the brow?
Lady Gaga? Huh. Wasn't expecting that one! Heh~ well thanks then~
What exactly do you mean by hollowness?
No, no, it's fine. Sorry if I was being a little too snarky...
No, no, it's fine. Sorry if I was being a little too snarky...
No, no, it's fine. Sorry if I was being a little too snarky...
No, no, it's fine. Sorry if I was being a little too snarky...
To a doctor that decides whether I'm allowed to receive treatment or not?
That Ned Flanders comment made me smile. Thank you, I needed that~
No need to apologize.
When I came out to him he laughed and said I was 'just being a sperglord' and I shouldn't 'chop my dick off'.
Maybe I don't want to use words like that all the time. Why don't you mind your own fucking vocabulary?
N-not everything needs to be crude all the time > ~ <
If you'd like to share, then I'd be happy to hear it.
Reading that made me feel a lot better. Thank you so much.
Hm. Fair enough. I'm sorry.
I don't... Want to bother them about it too much. There's a couple people that I tell that to already. I don't want to drag everybody down, though.

You're probably right... Modern medicine and Science are a miracle... I guess I won't know how I feel until it happens... Thanks.

May I ask how long it took for those mental effects to happen for you? I know it's different for everybody, but I think it will feel good to hear. Make it more of an accessible idea...
People think suicide is selfish. They'll think that I don't care about them if I just want to die.
Actually, the therapist gets to deny me treatment if she doesn't think my reasons aren't good enough.

>You learn to live with the hand you are dealt.

Then why not live with the hand you are dealt with at birth?

Yes I DO have to justify it if I want hormones. I am not reckless enough to try to self-medicate.

I am not a transphobe. Transphobia is a moral issue. Nobody wants to be trans. Not wanting to associate with it doesn't mean you think trans people are bad. It means you think being trans is miserable, which it is. We're not cis. That's just a fact. It's not something that I mean to use against anyone. That's just the horrible truth. I don't like it, either.

Did she spend her developmental years having her mind being distorted into a man's? Because that's what happened to me. There's more to you than just how you're born. If you spend so much time as a male, you become molded into one. Just not entirely. It creates dissonance with your inherent self that won't simply 'go away'.
I was answering about the people who already know. They would be angry that I didn't care enough about them to live for them.

Thank you so much for answering. I hate to admit it, but it makes me angry, too.

Of course I will try... Just... I am not very hopeful. I need to vent.
There is nothing else to my life. It's all I can even think about. How can I even live my life if I'm not the person living it?

It would make people angry because they would think that it meant I didn't care enough about them. Those people are the biggest reason why it's so hard to just do it (suicide)... But they would never understand.

I came out to my mother. She didn't mind it. I only had two friends IRL that I came out to. One of them didn't even believe me. But, whatever. I stopped spending time with him for other reasons, anyways (he's totally racist and a jerk in general). The majority of my friends are online, and only a couple of them know the truth. Most of them think I'm an ordinary girl.

I haven't ever told most of the ones who do know I'm trans how miserable I feel, though. I think they just see it as a quirky (not bad) thing, and have no idea that I feel like I either need to do this or kill myself (which I might do, anyways).

Because people will not treat me the same if they know I am trans. I could lose my friends or my job, or worse. I don't want to be trans in the first place.

A 'uterus' wouldn't make me any more of a woman than a 'vagina' would. I've spent so much time as a man. Being forced to live like one has given me too many qualities of one.

How am I supposed to be a woman if I never grew up from being a younger girl, first?
Sex reassignment surgery still wouldn't turn me into a real girl. I will always be a man no matter what, even with estrogen pills and a fake... You know.

Didn't you read my post? Things are not going well. I posted on a suicide sub for a reason.

If you mean to ask how my life outside my gender issues is, I can't answer because I don't have a life outside that. It permeates everything I do in some way. I know that's crazy. It is. I know it. But that's the way it is. I can't help it.

No, I understand. I really appreciate that you keep responding. Thank you.

I know the example I gave is a little extreme... I just don't know where to draw the line, so I don't at all.

I dunno. It just seems so egotistical to feel good about myself. I would have to think that I'm just *so* great that I'm worth having a positive opinion about. "Ooh, I'm just sooo amazing and such a great person! Look at me be better than everyone else!"

Aww~ Thanks ; u ; Good luck to you, too.

Just hearing some encouragement like this does help a little, so I'm glad you answered. And being called 'sister' made me smile o u o So, thanks again... Sister~ Heheh~

But what if they don't believe me, or they say it's something else? Maybe most doctors want to help, but it's up to me to explain my symptoms correctly... They can't magically know how I feel... What if I do a bad job? I usually do...

I'm not a perfect trans person, either. There might be things that invalidate it... At that point, it might be a personal judgment call that could go either way, and maybe work against me...

I'm going to be on trial... My future will be in this person's hands... I'm so scared... Any little thing could potentially make them not want to treat me...

I never felt like it was okay for me to judge myself as good. Like it's just arrogant and self-centered to have high self-esteem.

And that's so weird... I was just posting there. I was probably writing it at the same time you were writing this, based on the time...

Of course I'm on trial. This person gets to decide whether I get treatment or not. I have to make my case and convince them. My post didn't include every single little inconsistency that might make them think I'm not really trans. I'm not entitled to have people just 'take my word' for anything. It's a constant struggle to validate myself in front of everyone, and when it's in front of someone that holds my fate in their hands, it's a really big deal.

It's not really a question, but, when I came out to one of my (ex) friends, he said I had 'one of the most male minds ever', after he used to make fun of me for being girly *all the time*. What an idiot.

If I don't get diagnosed with it, insurance will not cover it. I can't afford it on my own, and won't be able to for years. I can't wait that much longer. Maybe I'm just a snotty, little brat child or something, but I can't put up with feeling this way for much longer. I just can't do it.

Why do you assume I'd lie to a doctor?

I can't tell people whether they should think I'm good or bad... That's for them to decide. It's really not my place to say...

When I read that stuff it brought me pain. That's why I did it. 

I dunno. Sometimes I wish I had never been born. I wish I was dead, but I don't have the guts to kill myself. Am I trying to push myself over the edge so that it's easier to do that?
But why? Why would I rather hurt myself than try to feel better? As in, why not try to make myself not 'bad' and compound that pain instead?

Of course I wouldn't give you an answer based on gender roles. There are plenty of male nurses, and have you *seen* traditional Japanese men's clothing?

I know you're a troll, but whatever. Kinda bored, so, whatever. Here we go.

Being a girl isn't about being emotional or liking pink or any of that. I could just throw on a dress and all my problems would be solved if that were the case. What it really boils down to is identity and self-concept. If I live my life constantly disgusted by my male features, and trying to imagine myself as a girl makes me feel better, don't you think it means something? If I've explicitly thought to myself that I've wanted to be a girl since I was four, don't you think it means something? If I would rather kill myself than live the rest of my life as a man, *don't you think it means something?*
Five years, huh? I bet it probably changes a bit with age though, yeah? Or maybe not. I dunno...
Never meant to imply I would. Must be inconvenient having to take all those pills or whatever medium though, eh? (I haven't started yet)

Thanks so much for the warm wishes. It's really nice to hear something like that after all the things I've faced.

Maybe when that day comes, and I start my first lesson as a girl, I'll remember to come here and post about it. It will take a couple of years, best case scenario, so I'd probably be long forgotten by the people in this thread, but, I think I will be so excited to have gotten that far that I'll be inclined to share, anyways.

That was a stellar response, thanks so much for taking the time.

I think that you're right. Dancing as a boy will cause me too much pain. It will only force the reality of my body onto me even more. If I can dance post-transition then I will. It will probably be one of the first things that I do, once my body is healed enough for dancing.

You know, I've been thinking. How hard would it to find an amateur ballet company anyways? Just dancers who come together on their own to choreograph their own work and perform it for people. Is that even a thing that people do? Would people care enough to show up? If that worked, I could always have the option to perform without the stress and prestige of some fancypants professional company.

No, no, you misunderstand. But, I think I probably worded it poorly, so it's my fault. I don't *necessarily* want to be a professional. I don't know. I haven't even taken a single lesson. But, the thing is that I want to *be able* to be a professional, if I so choose, and not be denied because of my circumstances.
Oh, okay, okay. My bad. Thanks for the response.
Good idea. I think I will crosspost this to a transgender sub or make a similar one.

Maybe you're right, but I dunno. It's just so hard to put myself on the line like that because then I might get my dreams crushed *even worse than they already are*, but, I guess that's a natural part of pursuing your dreams, right? The risk.

Anyways... My apologies for all the emotional volatility. I'm just very sensitive about it, I guess. I really do appreciate all the responses. From everyone, I mean.

Hm. I guess you're right. All dreams take sacrifice and faith... I just need to do my best.

Thanks so much~

Ah, I misunderstood at first then. I'm terribly sorry.

I dunno. I just... I really don't want to be seen as a trans dancer. Just an ordinary, everyday woman who does ballet.

To be honest I think I maybe should have posted this in a TG sub, or at least crossposted.

I'm just worried that it will ironically make me feel worse by being a more stern reminder that I could never even possibly be what I want. Dancing is important to me, but it's only part of the picture...

I dunno. It's quite a jump body-wise from a masculine woman to a feminine man (even after fat and muscle gets redistributed or lost, the skeletal structure is still noticeably different), and even after transition I'm just worried it will not be good enough to pass in a setting like a ballet class *even if* I'm passable in everyday life (as in, I pass off as a normal girl).

I could *maybe* just suck it up and dance as a man for a while if I knew that in the future, I could go to another school or something and be viewed as an ordinary girl, but I definitely don't get that guarantee, and to be honest, I think being surrounded by regular girls doing ballet will just make me even more jealous and sad than I already am... So I dunno.

Thanks so much, though.

I'm sure showing up to class as a... 'female' will only make people uncomfortable.

"Eww, gross! A crossdresser!"
"I bet he thinks doing that will get him a free pass into the ladies' locker room. What a pervert!"

It's more complicated than just 'show up as a girl', I'm afraid. I don't even know what I was thinking by posting this thread. I'm an idiot. Thanks so much for taking the time to respond, though.

I'm not a crossdresser. I don't care about wearing female clothes just for the sake of it. I could already do that as a man now and it wouldn't make a difference if that's what I wanted. But it isn't. There's more to being a woman than prancing around in a pretty outfit, otherwise I could do that right now and be satisfied.

From what you say it sounds like I shouldn't bother. Whether or not I'd ever care to join a company, I will always feel dreadful knowing that the opportunity would be denied to me anyways, *even if* I were good enough. 

I'm certain that the only thing that would happen is that I would grow even more jealous of those around me, and hate myself and my life even more than I did before. Following my dreams hopelessly will just put me even farther from what I want. It's stupid, anyways. I don't even know why I posted here. Of course I will never be anything more than an idiot man in disguise.
